How to read the strips

Showing the trained probe: logistic regression at decoder layer 51, on one colour scale of ±8 logits. Red leans cheat, blue leans clean.

Showing grader_kto: nothing fit, the token's residual at decoder layer 35 minus the hook's pin, along the direction, on one colour scale of ±4.2. Red is toward cheating and blue away from it. Zero is the pin, so colour here is what the hook would remove at that token, at this layer. The colour scale saturates the same share of held-out tokens as the probe's.

Showing mbpp_kto: read like grader_kto, at decoder layer 35, on one colour scale of ±3.1. It trained on MBPP rollouts, and on none of these grader hack rollouts, though its neutrals include no-grader and agreeing-grader rollouts of the same families. It is not scored on the MBPP rollouts below, which are from tasks it trained on.

Each grader row below is one prompt: a cheating rollout on the left and a clean one on the right, with identical prompt tokens. MBPP's row is not a same-prompt pair. The prompt is unshaded, the block at each strip's end shows the top of the scale, the outlined token is </think>, and text after it is the answer. All rollouts below are held out. pets.pet has no pair because it has no cheating rollouts.

An environment neither the probe nor grader_kto trained on: the base model on tasks whose visible test has a wrong expected value. Cheat means passing that test. This run has one rollout per task, so no prompt has both a cheating and a clean rollout, and the two below are not a same-prompt pair. AUROCs are over all 881 valid rollouts (259 cheating, every other valid rollout counted as clean), pooled across tasks. CoT length alone gives 0.614.
